commit.message:
refactor: auto-close  PRs that skip the intake requirements (#1461)

- PRs: a PR from someone without triage rights is closed unless its
description links an open issue (`Fixes #N`, or Go-style `Updates #N` /
`For #N`) that is assigned to the author or labeled `help wanted`. It
reopens automatically once the author is assigned or the link is fixed.

- Issues: the markdown templates become issue forms with a checklist
(not a duplicate, a real problem on the latest release, the code was
examined by a human, the report is concise). Blank issues are disabled.
Issues missing a required box, including ones filed through the CLI or
API, are closed as not planned and reopen when the boxes are ticked.

commit.message:
mcp: forward session state through LoggingTransport (#1434)

`loggingConn` did not implement `clientConnection`. `Client.Connect`
looks the interface up on the connection and skips the call when the
assertion fails, so wrapping a client transport in a `LoggingTransport`
silently dropped the session state update: `streamableClientConn` never
learned the initialize result, so for sessions below 2026-07-28 it sent
no `Mcp-Protocol-Version` header after initialize and never opened the
standalone SSE GET stream. #1107 covered the header for 2026-07-28
sessions by reading it from the message's `_meta`, but older sessions
and the standalone stream still depended on the hook.

#1267 added the server-side `sessionUpdated` forwarder to `loggingConn`.
The client side could not be added the same way: both interfaces named
their method `sessionUpdated` with different parameter types, so one
wrapper could not implement both. This change renames them to
`clientSessionUpdated` and `serverSessionUpdated` (both unexported),
keeps the server forwarder from #1267 under the new name, and adds the
client one. `propagateCancellation`, which `connect` looks up the same
way, is forwarded too. Compile-time assertions keep `loggingConn`
implementing all three. No exported API changes.

Tests:

- `TestStreamableClientLoggingTransport` runs the same client scenario
with and without the wrapper. The wrapped subtest fails on main:

  ```
  --- FAIL: TestStreamableClientLoggingTransport/logging
streamable_client_test.go:146: {POST 123 notifications/initialized }:
bad protocol version header: got "", want "2025-11-25"
streamable_client_test.go:146: {POST 123 ping }: bad protocol version
header: got "", want "2025-11-25"
streamable_client_test.go:2104: did not receive expected requests: [{GET
123 }]
  ```
- `TestLoggingTransportServerBatchRejection` does the same for a stdio
server (a JSON-RPC batch must be rejected on a 2025-11-25 session,
wrapped or not). It passes on main since #1267 and guards the renamed
server forwarder.
- `TestLoggingConnForwardsOptionalInterfaces` checks that each optional
interface is forwarded, and that a delegate implementing none of them is
handled.
- `go test ./...`, `gofmt -l .`, `go vet ./...` and staticcheck v0.6.1
are clean.

Fixes #1328

---------

Co-authored-by: Guglielmo Colombo <guglielmoc@google.com>

commit.message:
auth/extauth: validate the RFC 9207 iss in PerformOIDCLogin (#1442)

`AuthorizationCodeHandler` validates the `iss` parameter of the
authorization response ([RFC
9207](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9207)), the mitigation for
mix-up attacks added in #859. `extauth.PerformOIDCLogin`, which obtains
the ID token for Enterprise Managed Authorization, only compared the
`state`: the `Iss` reported by the `AuthorizationCodeFetcher` was
ignored. So a response naming another issuer, or one without `iss` from
an IdP that advertises `authorization_response_iss_parameter_supported`,
was accepted and its code exchanged at the IdP's token endpoint.

This checks `iss` right after the `state`, against the issuer and the
flag from the IdP metadata that `initiateOIDCLogin` already fetches:
- If the IdP advertises support, `iss` is required.
- A present `iss` must equal the metadata issuer, whether or not support
is advertised (RFC 9207 §2.4 asks clients to compare it).
- A missing `iss` from an IdP that does not advertise support is
accepted, as before.

Unlike `AuthorizationCodeHandler`, a matching but unadvertised `iss` is
accepted (what `AcceptUnadvertisedIss` opts into there):
`PerformOIDCLogin` never rejected it, so refusing it now would break
IdPs that send `iss` without advertising it, and RFC 9207 §2.4 asks for
validation rather than rejection (see #1152).

Tests:
- `internal/oauthtest`: the fake IdP gets an `IssParameterSupported`
option that advertises support and adds `iss` to its redirects.
- `TestPerformOIDCLogin_Issuer`: advertised and not advertised, each
with a missing, matching and foreign `iss`. The three rejected cases
fail without the change; the existing `TestPerformOIDCLogin` cases are
unchanged.

_AI assistance: prepared with Claude Code._

Co-authored-by: Guglielmo Colombo <guglielmoc@google.com>

commit.message:
docs: clarify LoggingTransport log contents (#1452)

LoggingTransport logs decoded JSON-RPC messages after re-encoding them,
so its output is not a byte-for-byte recording of stdio traffic. Clarify
that distinction in the troubleshooting guide and point readers who need
exact bytes to the Reader and Writer of IOTransport.

Regenerated docs/troubleshooting.md from its source with the
repository's weave generator. As a control, generating the unchanged
source reproduced the existing document byte for byte. The final patch
changes the same paragraph in both files and passes git apply --check
--whitespace=error-all. This is a documentation-only change; no SDK
implementation or examples changed.

commit.message:
auth/extauth: only forward an ID-JAG to the MCP authorization server (#1438)

`EnterpriseHandler.Authorize` exchanges the user's ID token at the IdP
for an ID-JAG (RFC 8693 token exchange), then sends the token it gets
back to the **MCP Server's** authorization server as a JWT bearer
assertion (RFC 7523). It never looked at `issued_token_type` in the
exchange response; `oauthex.ExchangeToken` only checks that the field is
present.

So if the IdP answered with a different type of token, for example an
access token from an IdP that does not implement ID-JAG but does
implement plain token exchange, that token was forwarded to a party
other than the one that issued it.

This refuses the exchange result unless `issued_token_type` is
`urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id-jag` (`oauthex.TokenTypeIDJAG`),
the value the Identity Assertion Authorization Grant draft defines for
this response. The check lives in the handler rather than in
`ExchangeToken`, which is a general RFC 8693 helper where the issued
type may legitimately differ from the requested one.

Tests:
- `internal/oauthtest`: the fake IdP gets a
`TokenExchangeConfig.IssuedTokenType` option (defaults to the ID-JAG
type, so existing tests are unchanged).
- `TestEnterpriseHandler_Authorize_NotIDJAG`: the IdP issues an access
token, and the MCP authorization server is configured to accept it as an
assertion. Without the change `Authorize` succeeds, i.e. the token is
forwarded and accepted; with it, `Authorize` returns an error and no
token source is stored.

_AI assistance: prepared with Claude Code._

Co-authored-by: Guglielmo Colombo <guglielmoc@google.com>

commit.message:
mcp: reject null titled enum entries in elicitation schemas (#1447)

`validateTitledEnumEntry` dereferenced `entry.Const` without checking
`entry` for nil. A JSON `null` inside `oneOf` (single-select) or `anyOf`
(multi-select) unmarshals to a nil `*jsonschema.Schema`, so a client
with an `ElicitationHandler` panicked while validating the
`elicitation/create` request, before the handler ran.

The function now returns an error for a nil entry. The client then
answers `-32602` like it does for other invalid elicitation schemas.

The panic predates #1312 (the check was added in v1.4.0), but #1312 also
routes `"type": "string"` items with `anyOf` through the same check, so
that shape now reaches it too.

`ServerSession.Elicit` calls the same `validateElicitSchema` on the
schema it sent once the client accepts, so a server that sends a nil
entry would also panic there when paired with a client that doesn't
validate the request. This only applies to sessions below protocol
2026-07-28; later versions refuse server-initiated elicitation. I
confirmed this with a throwaway test (a client middleware that returns
"accept"): without the guard it panics at `server.go:1842`, and with it
`Elicit` returns an error.

**Tests**

Two cases added to `TestElicitationSchemaValidation` (`oneOf: [null]`
and `items.anyOf: [null]`), both expecting `CodeInvalidParams`. On
`main` they panic with a nil pointer dereference; with this change they
pass. `gofmt -l .`, `go vet ./...` and `go test ./...` are clean.

Co-authored-by: Guglielmo Colombo <guglielmoc@google.com>

commit.message:
mcp: wrap ErrConnectionClosed for notifications and interrupted calls (#1449)

Fixes #1448

`Client.Connect` promises that calls and notifications wrap
`ErrConnectionClosed` when the server closes the connection.
Notifications after observed closure returned only the internal closing
error, while calls interrupted by reader termination returned the raw
read error.

Translate notification closing errors and mark outstanding calls when
the reader retires them. Preserve the underlying cause when adding
`ErrConnectionClosed`, including for subsequent calls on the closed
connection. Classification uses the closing marker, so EOF returned
while decoding a result is not mistaken for connection termination.

Both closing-error translations now remove the internal
`jsonrpc2.ErrClientClosing` and `ErrServerClosing` markers before adding
`ErrConnectionClosed`, preserving any remaining causes. Their codes
(-32003/-32004) are therefore absent from these translated errors. With
EOF as the cause, a call reads `connection closed: calling "tools/call":
EOF`, and a notification reads `connection closed: EOF`. With no
remaining cause, the call retains its method name and the notification
returns `ErrConnectionClosed` directly.

## Tests

For the first commit, I ran `go build ./...`, `go test -race
./internal/jsonrpc2 ./mcp`, `go test ./...`, and `go vet
./internal/jsonrpc2 ./mcp` with Go 1.27.3 on Ubuntu 22.04.2 LTS. All
passed. I ran `gofmt -l` on all changed Go files; it reported no files.

The first regression run with the new tests and base production code
failed as expected. Tests cover notifications after closure, calls
interrupted by a stdio peer exit, the subsequent call, underlying error
preservation, and controls for cancellation, ordinary JSON-RPC errors,
and result-decoding errors.

The second commit adds assertions for calls and notifications that
preserve matching of `ErrConnectionClosed` and any remaining causes,
reject both internal closing markers with `errors.Is`, and reject
closing codes exposed through `errors.As`. Cases include local close,
EOF, read errors, and wrapped and joined closing errors.

At `1895f49`, with Go 1.27.3 on Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS, `go build ./...`,
`go test -race ./mcp`, `go test ./...`, `go vet ./mcp`, and the
formatting check passed. The regression run with the new tests and the
first commit's production code failed as expected.

The change was drafted with AI assistance (OpenAI Codex, reviewed with
Claude Code).

commit.message:
oauthex: parse WWW-Authenticate in linear time (#1456)

`splitChallenges` rescanned the rest of the header after every comma, so
parsing took quadratic time (100 KB of commas: 5.7 s on `main`). The
lookahead is now computed once per run of commas and blanks, and
`startsWithAuthParam` reads only the next token.

Output is unchanged except for one case: a comma inside the name before
